chk_problem.label: accurate
chk_problem.poster_evidence: Functional decline is often recognized only after falls, gait impairment, or reduced mobility become visible. Routine biomarkers may deteriorate earlier without triggering alerts. Existing tools capture one timepoint, while biomarker trajectories may reveal an earlier prevention window.
chk_problem.reason: The poster describes the problem of late recognition of functional decline and the potential of biomarker trajectories to identify an earlier prevention window under the 'Clinical Need' section.

chk_method.label: accurate
chk_method.poster_evidence:
Twelve prespecified biomarkers were modeled over a three-year window, with all post-index measurements excluded.
Baseline used biomarker means; trajectories captured variability, first-to-last change, measurement count, and daily slope.
Penalized logistic regression, random forest, XGBoost, and LightGBM were compared by five-fold cross-validation in N = 297,861.
chk_method.reason: The poster describes the feature engineering of trajectory descriptors (variability, first-to-last change, count, daily slope) and the machine learning models compared under 'Trajectory Modeling'.

chk_data.poster_evidence: Table 1: Model performance (3-year window, 5-fold CV, OOF; N = 297,861; 11.1% cases).

chk_setup.label: accurate
chk_setup.poster_evidence:
Penalized logistic regression, random forest, XGBoost, and LightGBM were compared by five-fold cross-validation in N = 297,861.
Missing values used training-fold medians; evaluation covered out-of-fold discrimination, calibration, and reclassification.
chk_setup.reason: The poster details the five-fold cross-validation setup, out-of-fold evaluation, and comparison of the four machine learning algorithms.

chk_baseline.poster_evidence:
Trajectory features outperformed static summaries: AUROC 0.797 versus 0.755 and AUPRC 0.380 versus 0.304.
Age and sex matching yielded AUROC 0.727 versus 0.680 for demographics alone.

chk_conclusion.label: accurate
chk_conclusion.poster_evidence: Trajectory features outperformed static summaries: AUROC 0.797 versus 0.755 and AUPRC 0.380 versus 0.304. Precision-recall performance achieved a 25% relative improvement at 11.1% prevalence. Signal persisted up to 12 months before diagnosis, enabling zero-burden preventive monitoring.
chk_conclusion.reason: The poster concludes that trajectory features significantly improve prediction and can enable zero-burden preventive monitoring.
